conventions.convention: Both momentum procedures initialize w₀ = w₁ = w_init and perform updates for t = 1,…,T−1; T = 1 performs no updates.
Heavy-ball evaluates the gradient at the current iterate, with constant α > 0 and β ≥ 0.
Nesterov evaluates the gradient at w_t + β_t(w_t − w_{t−1}); α_t > 0 and β_t are prescribed real sequences.

The heavy-ball factor is the maximum modulus of characteristic roots, minimized over the entire interval [c,L], rather than a one-step Euclidean contraction or a worst case restricted to the actual spectrum.
For c < L, repeated endpoint roots permit linear polynomial prefactors; for c = L, the tuned polynomial is r² and its root factor is zero.
The reported stochastic comparison concerns training errors under a specific experimental setup and asserts no general convergence rate or test-risk guarantee.

load_bearing.statement: For a continuously Fréchet differentiable F: ℝᵈ → ℝ, initialize w₀ = w₁ = w_init and set w_{t+1} = w_t − α∇F(w_t) + β(w_t − w_{t−1}) for t = 1,…,T−1, with α > 0 and β ≥ 0.

For a real symmetric positive-definite quadratic whose eigenvalues lie in [c,L], 0 < c ≤ L, the parameters α = 4/(√L + √c)² and β = q², where q = (√L − √c)/(√L + √c), give modal root factor q throughout [c,L] and minimize the interval worst-case root factor among constant α′ > 0, β′ ≥ 0. Gradient descent with step 2/(L+c) has interval factor (L−c)/(L+c), strictly larger when c < L.
Initialize w₀ = w₁ = w_init. For t = 1,…,T−1, set the look-ahead point ŵ_t = w_t + β_t(w_t − w_{t−1}), then w_{t+1} = ŵ_t − α_t∇F(ŵ_t), with prescribed α_t > 0 and real β_t.

concerns.concern: The setup description says they used a slowly increasing momentum schedule capped by μ_max, but omits the final reduction to 0.9 for the last 1,000 updates (except the zero-momentum baseline). The primary source, https://proceedings.mlr.press/v28/sutskever13.pdf, PDF p. 5, §3 following Table 2, explicitly describes this finishing phase; Table 2 distinguishes the resulting Curves error 0.074 from the pre-finetuning value 0.096. The reported Table 1 numbers are correct, but the experimental procedure needs this qualification.
